threats.scenario: A client spoofs actor/scope/confirmation or uses an object ID to cross workspace, journey, party or traveller boundaries.
preconditions: An authenticated or OAuth client can submit another object UUID, stale version, forged client context or confirmation claim.

threats.scenario: A policy gap, direct adapter write or RLS mismatch exposes or mutates data outside the evaluated scope.
preconditions: A route, worker or query can reach PostgreSQL using an application role and malformed/missing transaction-local scope.

threats.scenario: A custom role, transitive party relationship or delegation grants permissions the actor does not hold.
preconditions: A role administrator can edit definitions/assignments while principals have overlapping workspace, journey, party or traveller relationships.

threats.scenario: An operator uses standing privilege, weak reauthentication or an unaudited export to access customer content.
preconditions: A platform/support operator has privileged credentials and can initiate or influence a customer-support case/session.

threats.scenario: Stale sessions or an offline client retain data after access is revoked or reintroduce it through a conflict.
preconditions: A formerly authorized client is offline or retains an active session/cache/wrapped key when policy changes.

threats.scenario: A user misunderstands provider processing/retention or an entitlement is mistaken for authority.
preconditions: An authenticated user chooses a provider/mode and submits prompts that cause policy-filtered context to leave Trax.

threats.scenario: A key leaks through database, logs, backups, support access, cross-workspace lookup or runtime memory.
preconditions: A router workload can resolve opaque secret references while database, logs, backups, support and other workspaces cannot.

threats.scenario: SSRF, DNS rebinding, redirects, alternate IP forms or headers reach private/metadata services or exfiltrate context.
preconditions: A workspace user can configure a URL/header and the egress adapter resolves/connects/follows redirects or streams responses.

threats.scenario: Redirect abuse, code/token interception, refresh replay or audience confusion impersonates or over-scopes a user.
preconditions: An external client can register/use redirect URIs, start authorization, hold codes/tokens and call a resource audience.

threats.scenario: Schema injection, represented-user confusion or an adapter-specific write bypasses policy/change/audit.
preconditions: An OAuth/Atlas client supplies resource IDs and typed tool arguments to the MCP adapter under represented-user scopes.

threats.scenario: A changed/stale proposal, replayed approval or race executes more than the user reviewed.
preconditions: A model can propose payloads while records, permissions or consent change before a user approves/executes.

threats.scenario: Prompt injection, SSRF or fabricated/misleading citations broadens tools or makes untrusted content trusted state.
preconditions: A model controls page/candidate text and URLs while the fetcher/parser and reviewer process untrusted evidence.

threats.scenario: Cache reuse, raw arguments or observability leaks context across principals, parties or providers.
preconditions: Caches, audit emitters and telemetry receive principal/provider/tool metadata during model and MCP operations.

threats.scenario: Prompts, streaming responses, redirects, candidate batches or fetched pages consume egress sockets, tokens, CPU, memory or verification queues.
preconditions: An authorized model user, malicious provider or submitted URL can trigger repeated, slow, oversized or highly redirected work.

threats.scenario: A compromised client, incorrect crypto framing or plaintext staging exposes a sensitive document to server/storage.
preconditions: Sensitive plaintext exists in client memory and the encryption implementation chooses framing, randomness, keys and staging locations.

threats.scenario: Key substitution, replay or a revoked/incorrect target device receives a decryptable replica.
preconditions: A sender/server/device can publish or select device public keys and create/download a transfer for a target replica.

threats.scenario: XSS, browser cache/service worker, relay confusion or session replay persists or redirects plaintext.
preconditions: The web runtime can run application/third-party code and negotiate a server-mediated viewing session after device approval.

threats.scenario: Polyglot/archive malware, scanner failure, signed-URL overreach or TOCTOU makes unverified content available/current.
preconditions: An authenticated user can upload adversarial bytes and receive signed operations while scanner/object version state changes asynchronously.

threats.scenario: Metadata, counts, checksums or telemetry reveal identity/health/document facts across parties or to models/support.
preconditions: Authorized APIs, support, Atlas/MCP, telemetry and backups can observe policy-filtered metadata fields and aggregate counts.

threats.scenario: Failed/idempotency-broken cleanup leaves undeclared copies or logs deleted payloads as evidence.
preconditions: Retention jobs can access database/object/transfer identifiers and delete across stores while backups expire separately.

threats.scenario: Many files, archives, decompression bombs or abandoned signed uploads consume object storage, scanner CPU/memory or quarantine capacity.
preconditions: An authenticated uploader can obtain upload operations or submit content crafted to expand processing cost within or around declared limits.

threats.scenario: An attacker abuses credentials, enumerates accounts, fixes or steals a session, or forges a state-changing request.
preconditions: The public register/login/logout routes are reachable; the attacker has guessed credentials, a stolen cookie, or a cross-site request opportunity.

threats.scenario: A storage or application flaw exposes credentials, accepts forged session state, or fails to revoke a session.
preconditions: The attacker can exploit the authentication service/database role or obtain a credential/session datastore copy.

threats.scenario: An attacker replays or intercepts recovery material, enrolls a factor, or exploits a weaker recovery path to take over an account.
preconditions: The attacker controls or observes mailbox, MFA/recovery enrollment, recovery codes, or a privileged user support interaction.

threats.scenario: A replayed or misbound invitation/pairing claim links the wrong principal or grants broader workspace access.
preconditions: The attacker possesses an invitation/pairing artifact and can race, replay or present it while linking an identity.

threats.scenario: A recovery or invitation token, recipient address, party-private detail or security message is sent to the wrong recipient, exposed in provider telemetry, or reused as proof of activated access.
preconditions: An attacker can influence recipient selection/template context, compromise a mailbox/provider, or obtain a delivered single-purpose link.

threats.scenario: Automated registration/login attempts consume Argon2 CPU, database connections or session storage and deny legitimate authentication.
preconditions: The public authentication endpoints are reachable and an attacker can send sustained parallel requests or many distinct account identifiers.

threats.scenario: Device theft, shared OS access or an unlocked compromised endpoint lets another person act as the local principal.
preconditions: An attacker obtains the device, shares the OS account, bypasses local unlock, or runs code in the unlocked native process.

threats.scenario: Filesystem access, rollback or application compromise reads or silently modifies authoritative local records.
preconditions: An attacker can copy/replace database files, restore an older snapshot or exploit local persistence/migration code.

threats.scenario: Keys are exported through weak fallback storage, OS backup, debugging or a compromised unlocked runtime.
preconditions: An attacker can invoke key APIs from a compromised process, trigger fallback storage, inspect backups/debugging, or change device security state.

threats.scenario: OS backup or an unprotected export leaks data; a tampered or rollback import destroys or rewrites authority.
preconditions: A user or attacker can access OS backup settings, exported files, import selection or older valid exports.

threats.scenario: A malicious server/device impersonates pairing or silent last-write-wins loses or broadens local data.
preconditions: An attacker controls pairing discovery/channel/server identity or supplies conflicting local/cloud records during import.

threats.scenario: TLS/proxy/cookie/origin misconfiguration enables interception, forged client scheme/IP or cross-origin requests.
preconditions: A public deployment accepts TLS/proxy/host/origin/cookie configuration and untrusted internet traffic.

threats.scenario: Secrets leak through files, environment dumps, logs/backups or an overprivileged workload crosses service boundaries.
preconditions: Operators inject credentials/config into API, worker, database, object, sync, mail and provider workloads.

threats.scenario: Compromised/unavailable dependency, direct write path or overprivileged worker corrupts data or bypasses policy.
preconditions: API/workers call authenticated dependencies and process jobs after user transactions or provider events.

threats.scenario: Standing admin access, missing MFA/audit or unsafe exports enable undetected disclosure or mutation.
preconditions: An operator/support principal has infrastructure or break-glass privileges over centrally stored customer data.

threats.scenario: Unencrypted/overretained backups, untested restores or restoration of revoked/deleted data causes loss or disclosure.
preconditions: Backup systems copy central data/keys and operators later authorize restore into an environment with current policies.

threats.scenario: Dependency/artifact compromise, downgrade or incompatible migration breaks security or silently changes authority.
preconditions: Maintainers publish dependencies/artifacts/migrations and clients negotiate versions during deployment/update.

threats.scenario: A cloud-only dependency, private fork or entitlement check gates public functionality or becomes authorization.
preconditions: A deployment may configure optional Cloud hosting/model/backup/support while public clients consume versioned capabilities.

threats.scenario: Raw command arguments, prompts, document/health data, secrets or inaccessible party context enters telemetry; audit is weakened or overexposed; or non-essential telemetry ignores/obscures the required opt-out.
preconditions: An emitter can submit arbitrary fields, a schema/configuration change bypasses allowlists or opt-out state, or operators grant telemetry and audit the same readers/retention.

threats.scenario: An export includes inaccessible data, cancellation remains writable, a hold is broad or indefinite, purge misses a primary/object/backup copy, or restore resurrects deleted or revoked state.
preconditions: A user/operator can request export or lifecycle action, configure retention/hold policy, run purge, or restore a backup.

threats.scenario: A failing provider, poison job, retry loop or saturated database/object/scanner dependency causes workers to amplify load and starve public API operations.
preconditions: A dependency can become slow/unavailable or an attacker can create authorized work that repeatedly fails after commit.

threats.scenario: A token, subscription rule or service compromise sends records from another workspace or party.
preconditions: A device holds a sync credential and can request subscriptions while rules or token claims contain workspace/journey/party selectors.

threats.scenario: A rule/configuration error or privileged service role bypasses application/RLS isolation.
preconditions: A sync administrator/service role can publish rule changes or query PostgreSQL beyond application paths.

threats.scenario: A client alters actor/scope, replays IDs, collides idempotency keys or exploits conflict handling to bypass current policy.
preconditions: A client controls queued payloads, UUIDs, command IDs, expected versions, ordering and retry timing after disconnection.

threats.scenario: A permanently offline or hostile device retains previously authorized data and keys after revocation.
preconditions: A device retains cached rows/wrapped keys while offline when memberships, roles or grants are revoked.

threats.scenario: Vendor outage, licence restriction, unsafe upgrade or operator misconfiguration breaks self-host parity or isolation.
preconditions: An operator/vendor controls deployment, licence, sync rules, upgrades and administrative credentials.

threats.scenario: A client or compromised sync identity creates unbounded subscriptions, command retries, conflicts or tombstones that exhaust replication, upload or reconciliation capacity.
preconditions: A paired client can maintain subscriptions or submit many unique/retried commands and pathological conflict sequences.
